[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) using MySQL Binlogs"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) is a critical database administration strategy used to restore a MySQL database to a specific moment in time. This technique combines a full physical or logical backup with incremental binary logs (binlogs)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Configuration"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before performing PITR, binary logging must be enabled in your MySQL configuration file (my.cnf or my.ini). Ensure the following parameters are set under the [mysqld] section:"},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"[mysqld]
server-id = 1
log-bin = mysql-bin
binlog_format = ROW"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"server-id: A unique identifier for the MySQL server instance."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"log-bin: Enables the binary log and sets the base filename."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"binlog_format: Row-based replication ensures precise data changes are captured."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Taking a Full Baseline Backup"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"PITR always starts with a known good baseline backup. Use mysqldump to create a full backup and include the current binary log coordinates:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"mysqldump --all-databases --single-transaction --flush-logs --master-data=2 > full_backup.sql"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Simulating Data Loss and Identifying the Target Time"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Imagine an accidental drop table command or erroneous data modification occurs at 2023-10-25 14:30:00. Your goal is to recover the database right up to the second before this event."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Restoring the Full Baseline Backup"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, restore your database to the state it was in when the full backup was taken:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"mysql -u root -p < full_backup.sql"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Applying Binlogs Up to the Target Point"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Locate your active binary log files in the MySQL data directory. Use the mysqlbinlog utility to replay transactions up to your specific timestamp or log position."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"mysqlbinlog --stop-datetime="2023-10-25 14:29:59" /var/lib/mysql/mysql-bin.000002 | mysql -u root -p"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Alternatively, if you prefer using log positions for absolute precision, use the stop-position flag instead:"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"mysqlbinlog --stop-position=4523 /var/lib/mysql/mysql-bin.000002 | mysql -u root -p"},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"By following these steps, you can successfully recover your MySQL database to any exact moment in time, mitigating the impact of human error or application glitches."}]
